## Problem

When a ticket description exceeds the 8,000-character plan-review admission limit, the only
remediation offered is **decomposition**. `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py:347-350`:

```python
"suggested_fix": (
    f"Reduce the description to at most {desc_limit} characters, usually by splitting "
    "independent work into coherent child tickets."
),
```

That is the right advice when the **work** is too large. It is the wrong first advice when the
**prose** is too large, which is the more common cause — and an author who follows it fragments a
coherent unit of work for a reason that has nothing to do with its scope.

## Evidence

Measured on `darkish-enormous-raptors` (`76b2-4b5f-5682-45e5`), which hit the limit:

```
description at rejection : 7989 chars — 14 acceptance criteria, 105 lines of narrative prose
after rewriting prose out: 4440 chars — ALL 14 criteria retained, plus 9 required provenance lines
headroom under the limit : 3560 chars (44% spare)
```

**Nothing needed splitting.** The unit of work was one coherent cleanup with fourteen criteria. What
exceeded the limit was method discussion, rationale, and conversational progression that belonged in
ticket comments. Removing none of the commitments and none of the evidence — only relocating the
narration — left 44% headroom.

Had the author followed the suggested fix literally, they would have split a single cleanup into
child tickets to solve a formatting problem.

At least **two independent sessions hit this limit on 2026-08-20**, and both independently arrived
at the same unsuggested remedy: move the narrative into a comment. Two sessions rediscovering the
same fix that the message does not mention is the signal.

## Why this is a coaching defect and NOT a limit defect

Stated plainly, because this ticket replaces an earlier one of mine
(`piecemeal-batiste-greatargus`, closed `not_a_bug`) that got this wrong:

**8,000 characters is ample for one ticket's worth of work** — roughly 1,200 words. A plan that
cannot state its problem and its acceptance criteria in that space is either describing more than
one unit of work or is padded. The limit is correct and should not move. The formatting requirements
that share the budget (`provenance:` continuation lines) are also correct and fit comfortably.

The gap is that the message names one cause of over-length and one remedy, when there are two
distinct causes with different remedies, and the more common one is unaddressed.

## Direction (not a prescription)

Distinguish the two cases and coach accordingly. The signal is already available: this same function
computes `oversize signals` separately from `description_over_limit`, and its OTHER branch already
suggests G5 decomposition for genuinely large units. So decomposition advice already has a home;
the over-limit branch could instead coach on authoring:

- prefer concise language over narration;
- move conversational progression, method discussion, and rationale into ticket **comments** or a
  **session log** — the description carries the plan and its acceptance criteria;
- follow the packaged authoring guidance (`rebar explain plan`,
  `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md`);
- and only split when the WORK is genuinely more than one unit — pointing at the oversize-signal
  branch rather than conflating the two.

Whether to keep any mention of splitting in this branch is a judgement call for the implementer;
the defensible minimum is that it stops being the *only* suggestion.

## Relationship to other tickets

Same class as `bediasite-bilineate-stoat` (`fb8b-189d-97ab-4546`, closed): a gate message whose
stated remedy under-serves the situation the author is actually in. That one was fixed by making the
message name the consequence the author would otherwise discover the hard way. This is the same fix
shape applied to a different message.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The over-limit finding's `suggested_fix` names concision and relocating narration to comments
      or a session log as remedies, not only decomposition — verified by a test asserting the
      message content.
- [x] The message distinguishes CONTEXT that must stay (problem, constraints, acceptance
      criteria and their evidence — enough that a reader who has never seen the ticket can
      evaluate the plan) from NARRATION that should move to comments or a session log
      (investigation history, method discussion, conversational progression). Coaching that
      only says "be shorter" fails the completion verifier from the opposite direction and
      does not satisfy this criterion — verified by a test asserting both halves are named.
- [x] The message points at the packaged authoring guidance rather than restating it, so the advice
      cannot drift from the guide.
- [x] Decomposition advice remains available for the case it genuinely fits (a unit of work too
      large for one session) and is distinguishable from the over-length-prose case — verified by a
      test covering both branches.
- [x] The 8,000-character limit itself is UNCHANGED. This ticket does not raise it, and a change
      that raises it does not satisfy these criteria.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`
      (`new=0 increased=0 stale=0`) pass.
